hypothesis: Iter 94 = FIX THE INSTRUMENT, THEN MAKE SLOW PHYSIOLOGY LEARNABLE. Two measurements drove it. (1) iter-93's own primary criterion FAILS in the student, 0/4 bands: at the prior-mean embedding a 24 h fast gives glucose 90.3 (band 70-85), insulin 11.0 (2.5-6.5), FFA 0.56 (0.8-1.4), BHB 0.13 (0.8-2.2). The teacher was fixed and the student did not inherit it. (2) The gate could not have told us: on the 24 episodes it called 'real', carrying the last calibration reading forward scores glucose 0.0098 / hr 0.0141 / temp 0.0004 against thresholds 0.20 / 0.15 / 0.02 -- 11x to 50x looser, so a constant-output model passes everything. Zero of the 72 meals land in any scored window; temp ground truth has exactly two distinct values across all 168 points; 'source=real' was a code default, not an assertion. THREE ROOT CAUSES FIXED. (A) The ruler: legacy 24 tagged legacy_static, 14 real CGM+Oura overnight episodes added as cgm_real (4.6x more dynamic on glucose), 4 teacher_dynamic episodes whose SCORED window contains a meal, and skill_vs_persistence promoted from report line to gate metric at the natural zero. teacher_dynamic is excluded from the distillation pool so the gate is not trained on. (B) Slow physiology had ~1/3000th the gradient of meal physiology: the distillation anchor normalized residuals by each marker's GLOBAL NORM_SCALE, a scale meal excursions dominate, so a flat predictor paid 0.00055 on the fasting protocol vs 1.505 on the 3-meal protocol for glucose. Normalizing by the reference's own within-window range (floored at 5%) closes the visibility gap 43x -> 2.8x; long 480-min anchor windows score slow arcs as arcs; and the knowledge signals now get 25 epochs instead of 10 (enable_at is the phase boundary, so every literature-grounded signal ran only in epochs 50-59 of 60 at a decaying LR). (C) THE BIGGEST FINDING, and NOT what iter 93 predicted: GLYCOGEN COULD NEVER FALL BELOW ITS TYPICAL VALUE. The mass-action assembly is prod*prod_scale - cons*cons_scale*norm_state, and norm_state is ZERO at typical, so the entire breakdown term vanishes there while GlycogenFluxHead's prod is >= 0. Measured on the iter-93 artifact, both pools hit exactly min-typical = 0.0000 in EVERY protocol -- fasted, fed, and a 2 h hard bout -- while the teacher falls 58 g (liver) and 206 g (muscle). Liver glycogen was never a supervision problem and muscle was never a timescale problem; B alone would not have fixed either. Both pools now use an explicit flux balance in raw g/min with headroom/fullness gating, mirroring what glucose already does in the same forward. Plus the circadian family, re-scoped: teacher amplitudes brought to the literature the repo already cites (hrv_sleep_rise z +4.43 -> +0.99, sleep_hr_dip -2.87 -> -0.99, temp nadir -1.75 -> -0.37; contradictions 6/31 -> 4/31, every metabolic statistic byte-identical), and TEMP_CIRCADIAN_AMPLITUDE -- which was relu(0.5-amplitude), a ONE-SIDED FLOOR that made a 2x overshoot free -- now bands [0.5, 0.8]. REJECTED after measurement: hr_circ_amp 5.0->3.5 (no cohort statistic constrains it, and it does not achieve what it was invoked for -- whole-day contrast 26.7% vs 24.6%, both above the 10-20% band). Full detail and the six open items in docs/iter94-spec.md.
